description:
The Righteous Mind by Jonathan Haidt, explained in full: why your gut delivers a moral verdict in a split second and your reasoning only shows up afterward to defend it — and why that one fact divides good people over politics and religion.

There's a brother and sister, Julie and Mark, on summer vacation in France. One night, alone in a cabin near the beach, they decide — just out of nowhere — that it would be interesting to make love. Two forms of birth control, no one ever finds out, and they never do it again. It harms no one. So why are you certain it's wrong before you can say why?

That question is the whole of The Righteous Mind. Haidt's answer: intuitions come first, strategic reasoning second. Your reasoning is a press secretary hired after the fact to justify a decision it never made — which is exactly why arguments almost never change anyone's mind.

In this full summary and analysis you'll learn:
• Moral dumbfounding — why we "just know" something is wrong
• The elephant and the rider — how intuition really runs the show
• The inner press secretary that only asks "Can I believe it?"
• The WEIRD mind and its moral blind spot
• The six moral foundations that split left and right
• The hive switch — why we're 90% chimp, 10% bee
• Dawkins vs Durkheim — is religion a virus or the glue of groups?
• How to actually change a mind: talk to the elephant, not the rider

A clear, story-driven breakdown of one of the most important books in modern moral psychology. No fluff, no ending spoilers.
